transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Perez (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood CSM); Arun Patel (CTO, Summit AI), Sofia Martinez (Platform Eng), Ben Gold (Security Lead), Priya Rao (Product)
---
Summary:
Short kickoff/alignment to move Summit AI from trial to pilot: confirm pilot scope, security checklist, basic perf expectations, and next steps for private networking (VPC) and SSO. Multiple small transcription artifacts below.
Topics covered: pilot scope, VPC/on-prem options, SOC2 and audit logs, RBAC/SSO, performance benchmarks, success metrics, timeline to pilot.
---
Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? We have Maya, Lucas and Olivia from Redwood.
[00:00:12] Arun (Summit AI CTO): Arun here. Sofia, Ben and Priya with me. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:00:18] Maya: Awesome. Goal for today is just to align on pilot scope and the operational checklist so we can get you into a reserved pilot slot next week. Roughly 45 to 60 minutes, a bit more technical than a sales intro.
[00:00:30] Lucas (SE): Hi, quick note — I'll focus on the perf and infra bits. I pulled together a short benchmark plan which I'll share after the call.
[00:00:38] Sofia: Great. From our side we're especially interested in latency characteristics and ability to run inside our VPC. We have strict egress rules.
[00:00:45] Ben (Security): And encryption at rest/in transit plus KMS integration — that's non-negotiable for our legal.
[00:00:52] Olivia (CSM): I'll be tracking onboarding progress and runsheets, and making sure we have weekly check-ins.
[00:00:59] Maya: Perfect. Quick qualification: what's the primary success metric for pilot — latency or accuracy or cost savings?
[00:01:07] Priya (Product): For product it's our feature correctness and response consistency — we'll use a prompt set to validate. Business cares about latency under 300ms p50 for most calls. Cost is secondary for the pilot.
[00:01:20] Maya: Noted p50 300ms. Lucas, can Redwood meet that on a hosted setup?
[00:01:25] Lucas: Depends on model size and sequence lengths. For a 2k token average with one of our smaller llama-ish models, yes on hosted with continuous batching disabled for low-latency paths. If you need private deployment in VPC there's extra network hop — we'll see some delta.
[00:01:41] Arun: We prefer private plane — our compliance team won't let data hit public endpoints without private link. Can Redwood's Private option run inside our VPC?
[00:01:49] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package if needed. We'll need your network team to share CIDR and KMS owner contact — we'll put a template in the runbook.
[00:02:00] Ben: And audit logs? We need immutable audit trails for every API call.
[00:02:04] Lucas: We ship request-level audit logs. For private deployments we can route logs to your SIEM via a secure forwarder. Note: retention policy is configurable but shorter retention is on lower tiers.
[00:02:16] Ben: SOC 2?
[00:02:18] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — I'll attach the report. Also we can share our ISO and penetration test summaries.
[00:02:25] Sofia: Quick note — we will likely run canaries against existing OpenAI endpoints. How easy is it to switch traffic between hosted and private?
[00:02:33] Lucas: You can pin model version and route via policies. We support canary rollouts and A/B traffic splits in the console. There can be small config differences between cloud-hosted and private runtime, but we provide the same API surface.
[00:02:45] Priya: For cost modeling, do you provide per-token breakdowns by route?
[00:02:50] Olivia: Yes, console shows token-level cost and breakdown per route/model; we'll include expected unit economics in the benchmark doc.
[00:02:57] Arun: About latency again — do you do prefix caching or KV cache to speed up repeated prompts? We got someone saying KV cash but not sure.
[00:03:06] Lucas: Yes KV cache and prefix caching are supported; that can drastically lower cost and latency for chat-like flows — though it requires model and runtime support. We'll recommend configs in the Optimize playbook.
[00:03:18] Maya: I'm going to outline the pilot scope now: 1) Private VPC peering with dedicated reserved nodes for a two-week pilot; 2) Use Summit's 2k token prompt set and 1 eval suite; 3) Measure p50/p95 latency and tokens-per-call cost; 4) Check RBAC/SSO and audit log delivery; 5) Decide go/no-go at end of pilot. Thoughts?
[00:03:39] Arun: Sounds good. Two questions — what is the turnaround time to get a private env standing?
[00:03:44] Lucas: Typically 3-7 business days once we have network peering and credentials. If you need air-gapped on-prem package that expands timeline.
[00:03:52] Ben: Our KMS team uses a particular vendor and HSM — will Redwood integrate?
[00:03:56] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS via standard APIs. We'll confirm specifics in the security checklist.
[00:04:03] Priya: Any blockers on profiling inference cost at small scale? We want to estimate monthly spend for the pilot.
[00:04:09] Lucas: We'll run small-scale benchmarks and produce a token-cost projection. Need sample prompts and a representative concurrency pattern from you.
[00:04:18] Sofia: We'll send the prompt set after the call — two anonymized sets and one longer conversation thread.
[00:04:23] Maya: Great. I'll open up the onboarding runbook link — (link) — and drop a VPC template.
[00:04:29] [00:04:30] (brief cross talk, someone types link in chat)
[00:04:36] Maya: For SSO we support SAML/SCIM and OIDC. Ben, can you confirm which SSO provider you use?
[00:04:43] Ben: We're on Okta. SCIM is required for provisioning.
[00:04:47] Lucas: Okta SCIM is supported; we'll include the attribute map in the runbook. Some customers have custom RBAC needs — we can map groups to roles.
[00:04:57] Priya: How do you handle fallback if a model fails or latency spikes?
[00:05:02] Lucas: We have smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants and region fallbacks. For mission-critical paths we recommend a multi-model policy with a lower-cost fallback.
[00:05:10] Arun: Any examples of customers with similar constraints you can point to?
[00:05:14] Maya: We have a finance customer and a healthcare customer with private VPC setups — I'll share anonymized case notes and a short reference.
[00:05:21] Priya: About observability — can we trace back per-request tokens to function calls?
[00:05:26] Olivia: Our console/audit logs include token usage, latency, and model version per request. We also supply tracing hooks for your observability pipeline.
[00:05:34] Ben: One more: penetration testing window — if we want to run a black-box pen test against the private endpoint, what's the process?
[00:05:41] Lucas: We require a notice window and specific test plan. For private environments we'll coordinate with your security contact and ours; we can provide a test window.
[00:05:49] Maya: Let's capture agreed items. Olivia, want to list immediate run items?
[00:05:53] Olivia: Sure — I'll create the Confluence space. Action items: 1) Redwood to provide onboarding runbook, SOC2 and architecture notes; 2) Customer to provide prompt sets, VPC/KMS contact; 3) Redwood SE to run baseline perf; 4) schedule weekly syncs.
[00:06:11] Arun: Sounds right. One timeline ask — can we start the pilot environment by next Tuesday (2026-08-25)?
[00:06:17] Lucas: That's ambitious but possible if we get peering and KMS details today. Otherwise it slides a few days.
[00:06:24] Sofia: We'll prioritize network details.
[00:06:27] [00:10:00] (mid-call deeper technical dive, timestamps approximate)
[00:10:12] Lucas: Quick technical note about model quantization: for lower-cost profiles we can suggest 4-bit quantized variants; those trade a hair of quality for 2-3x cost reduction. For Summit's use-case you may want to test both.
[00:10:28] Priya: We'll want to run blind evals to verify quality loss isn't material.
[00:10:33] Lucas: Agreed. We'll include suggested prompts for that eval.
[00:10:39] Ben: On the logging side, does your immutable audit log support retention policies and export to S3?
[00:10:44] Lucas: Yes, for private we can forward logs to your S3 or SIEM and set retention. There's also aLedger-style append-only export if you need immutability. (note: transcription sometimes shows "a ledger" as "aleger")
[00:10:58] Maya: A few minor transcription artifacts here — ignore if words look odd.
[00:11:04] Maya: Anything else on security?
[00:11:07] Ben: Data residency — our legal says logs must remain in US regions.
[00:11:10] Maya: Noted, we'll ensure the private nodes and log forwarding are in the requested region.
[00:11:15] Sofia: How about rate limiting and quotas per API token?
[00:11:19] Lucas: Console supports per-token quotas and rate limits; we can implement burst policies.
[00:11:24] Priya: When do we lock model versions for pilot?
[00:11:27] Maya: We recommend pinning model version at pilot start and then use canary for rollouts after.
[00:11:32] Arun: Are the SDKs the same for private and hosted?
[00:11:35] Lucas: Yes, same SDKs. Some env config differs (endpoint url, certs), but API surface is identical.
[00:11:41] [00:20:00] (later in call, talk about pricing and commitments)
[00:20:07] Priya: For internal buy-in we'll need a conservative cost estimate for monthly run. Do you have a quick calc for 50k calls/month at our average tokens?
[00:20:15] Lucas: We'll run the numbers once we have exact token counts. For now I can provide a ballpark using two model tiers.
[00:20:21] Maya: We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up, with both hosted and dedicated variants.
[00:20:26] Arun: Any risks you foresee in the pilot?
[00:20:29] Maya: Biggest risk is network setup delays or missing KMS creds. Also if you want on-prem air-gapped we need more lead time.
[00:20:36] Sofia: We'll file the network request today.
[00:20:39] [00:30:00] (wrap-up phase)
[00:30:05] Olivia: Recap: Redwood to share runbook + SOC2 + VPC template; customer to share prompt sets + KMS contact; SE to run perf and cost projection; schedule weekly syncs.
[00:30:18] Maya: Any final questions?
[00:30:21] Ben: Only one — can you provide an anonymized diagram of private deployment?
[00:30:25] Lucas: Yes, I'll attach a diagram and a short step-by-step networking checklist.
[00:30:31] Priya: Thanks — excited to get started.
[00:30:34] Maya: Thanks everyone. Olivia will send meeting notes and invites.
[00:30:39] Arun: Appreciate it.
[00:30:41] (meeting ends)
